entry_points.text: Calls offer whole-system sync, full and data-only flush and two range variants via shared helper after validation plus early install of shared controls.

Write completes empty with zero else delegates to store; permission change merges bits; registration picks tables from hook presence with lock class and warns on duplicates; group ownership applies to directory then members with visibility checks.
Timer files validate clock and flags with wake privilege for alarms, program with spec validation reporting priors, query remaining and interval, and invalidate on clock-change waking waiters.

exports.text: Global recovery offers background emergency remount and thaw-all plus forward or reverse freeze and thaw walks using filesystem hooks when present else generic helpers with kernel holder.

Block supers are acquired by device, mounted with optional quiet lookup, torn down with block sync before holder release; holder files open by number or path; backing uses caller-named or sequenced objects; freeze prefers hooks and paths resolve.
Sync flushes inodes then filesystems then block devices with repeating background passes; range helper stages early wait, write and late wait in flag order.

Hierarchy management creates and removes directories with rename and relocation plus mount placeholders, installs and refreshes groups singly or as lists, and creates links under objects with warn and quiet variants plus remove and conditional rename.

File services create single and batched attributes with reverse rollback, add and remove group and namespaced entries including self removal, forward binary mmap seek and open to hooks, signal notification targets, format page output and serve simple private reads.

hazards.text: Async emergency work does nothing when allocation fails with thaw retries warning per attempt; resume defers to work context.
Mount placeholders and group links report collisions with namespaced deletion; vanished targets and directories need missing tolerance without held references.
Mount reuse flipping read-only warns and fails busy with frozen or read-only devices failing with diagnostics; oversize display truncates with warning and disabled removal reports unimplemented.

invariants.text: Active grab needs exclusive lock and nonzero count; device reuse needs equal devices with pointer or unconditional alternates; freeze keeps single errors and skips unsupported; tree reuses only on matching read-only and refuses read-only or frozen mounts.

Inode and filesystem passes skip read-only supers with filesystem sync also skipping no-sync or hookless entries in early and late passes; range sync rejects bad flags and offsets, clamps to cache limits and orders waits and writes by flags.

Directory creation fails without owner or parent, inherits parent or root, applies owner and warns on collision; device loss syncs unless surprise, shrinks names, evicts objects and shuts down absent veto, while periodic sync needs active rooted supers.

Preallocated read needs the open-file area, truncates oversize and drops prefixes before position; binary read clips to sized inodes needing a hook; binary write clips, rejects starts beyond end and needs a hook.

Disabled creation succeeds without action with removal noop, lookup null and removal unimplemented; live lookup and removal forward to namespaced forms; ownership updates via attribute change with link checks for type and target and object walks of default groups.

Null lists succeed; list creation and merge roll back on failure and missing removal logs; link creation rejects missing names or parents with detached as missing and duplicates as collision defaulting null parents to root while rename honours namespaces.

Start-time expiry counts triggered with remaining clamped at zero and absolute times translated; cancel applies only to realtime absolute cancel clocks with alarm versus timer by clock; ops verify ownership with wake privilege for alarms and reject bad flags and specs.

locks.text: Block binding updates serialize with a global lock and per-mount sync holds super read protection across filesystem sync merged with error-sequence advancement.

A spinlock serializes owner node clearing against target use; file helpers use read sections with node-lock asserts; active-protection break pairs object then leaf handling with unbreak resuming and releasing references.
A queue lock guards ticks and markers across trigger, poll and reprogramming; per-file and global guards protect cancel-list membership with read-side traversal and per-file locking for clock-change.

state_machines.text: Remount callback visits block-backed writable supers forcing read-only via fresh context then freeing it; registration reuses live entries under read protection else allocates and rechecks frozen with busy rollback.

Install skips empty groups deriving visibility from first visible member, creates directories when visible, populates files, removes newly invisible groups and drops new directories on failure with file removal support.

Timers move among disarmed, armed, expired-signalled and cancelled; expiry signals and ticks, consumption clears and may rearm periodic timers, and clock-change forces cancelled needing user re-evaluation with callback restart helpers.

structs.text: Holder ops bind loss, sync, freeze and thaw; shared controls expose bounded overflow identities; freeze masks combine kernel and userspace holders with nest and exclusive modifiers; diagnostics carry a fixed tag.

Tables encode empty, read-only, write-only and read-write for regular, preallocated and binary kinds with mapping adding mmap; population consults visibility, masks permissions and sizes binaries dynamically with rollback on failure.
Timer state holds dual timer, interval, offset marker, wait queue, ticks, clock id and linkage with guard; descriptor info and control may compile to null.

State holds shared root pointers, per-mount namespace tag with root and magic, free and tree ops, and type with name, setup, teardown and mount properties plus header guard; range mask combines three wait and write bits.
